episodes.187399: The strong low pressure system which approached the area on January 31 pulled up a deep surge of tropical moisture which brought moderate to heavy precipitation to much of the area on February 1 through the morning of February 2. Much of the San Joaquin Valley, West Side Hills and Tehachapi Mountains measured between 0.75 inches and 1.50 inches of rainfall while the Sierra Foothills picked up 1 to 2 inches of rainfall ands the higher elevations of the Sierra Nevada picked up 1.5 to 3 inches of liquid precipitation. The precipitation fell as snow above 6000 feet for much of this event with several higher elevation SNOTELs picking up an estimated 1 to 2 feet of new snow. In addition to the precipitation, there were several reports of wind gusts exceeding 60 mph near Tehachapi and in the Grapevine area during the early morning of February 1. When the main cold front from this system moved across central California during the afternoon of February 1, scattered thunderstorms broke out over the San Joaquin Valley and Sierra foothills. Some of the storms produced small hail and there were several reports of roadway flooding in Bakersfield. The precipitation tapered off by the morning of February 2.
episodes.187527: A strong atmospheric river brought damaging winds to northwestern California and flooding rains. Flooding lingered into February.
episodes.187539: A strong front brough widespread rain to Northwest California and damaging winds to portions of Del Norte and Humboldt counties. Small stream flooding was common across the region while main stem rivers also flooded in Mendocino County.
episodes.188034: A quick-moving cold front came through California on January 31, bringing widespread rain and high winds. A narrow cold frontal rainband (NCFR) developed during the afternoon and evening commute, with moderate to heavy rain across the region as a result. Impacts and post-frontal showers continued through February 1.
episodes.188036: A cold front came through California on January 31, bringing widespread rain and high winds. Impacts and post-frontal showers continued through February 1.
episodes.188706: Heavy rain brought flooding to several rivers in Arkansas in early February 2024.
episodes.188899: Well above normal rainfall along the Ohio River Valley in January led to rising rivers, with flood stage exceeded slightly at Shawneetown late January, continuing through the first week of February as drier weather allowed floodwaters to recede. Minor flooding resulted in very limited impacts in bottomland areas.
episodes.188900: Well above normal rainfall along the Ohio River Valley in January led to rising rivers, with flood stage exceeded slightly at Newburgh Dam and Mount Vernon late January, and J.T. Myers at midnight February 1st, continuing into the first week of February as drier weather allowed floodwaters to recede. Minor flooding resulted in very limited impacts in bottomland areas.
episodes.188901: Well above normal rainfall along the Ohio River Valley in January led to rising rivers, with flood stage exceeded slightly at Newburgh Dam, Mount Vernon, and Shawneetown late January, and J.T. Myers at midnight February 1st, continuing into the first week of February as drier weather allowed floodwaters to recede. Minor flooding resulted in very limited impacts in bottomland areas.
episodes.189034: An atmospheric river impacted Southern California on February 1st. Impacts were felt across much of the region, but the most notable impacts were near the Seal Beach area. Several reports of flooding leading to road closures were received from this area.
episodes.189402: The first powerful storm of February brought heavy rain, flooding, mountain snow and wind to the area. Across San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara counties, rainfall totals between 2 and 6 inches were reported which produced numerous reports of urban flooding. Across Ventura and Los Angeles counties, rainfall totals of 1 to 4 inches were reported along with some reports of flash flooding. In the mountains, winter storm conditions were observed with 2-5 inches of snowfall and wind gusts up to 69 MPH.
